claims.summary: For every 32-bit input, the export returns the sum of the integers below its unsigned value, reduced to 32 bits.
claims.reason: For every 32-bit input, the statement returns the sum of all unsigned values below it, reduced to 32 bits, as intended.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.sumTo
claims.intent: `sum_to(n)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: `0 + 1 + … + (n − 1)`, wrapped to 32 bits.
details: Input: one 32-bit value, interpreted as unsigned for the range bound.
The result is the sum of all integers from zero up to but excluding that value, reduced modulo 2 to the 32nd power; this is result wraparound, not signed arithmetic.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping, with exactly the specified result.
caveats: The claim uses the elaborated unsigned conversion of the input, so it covers every 32-bit input as a number from zero through the maximum unsigned 32-bit value; it does not read the input as signed.
The source notation for the sum is elaborated as the sum of the list of integers from zero up to, but not including, the input's unsigned value, then reduced to 32 bits.
The required examples field is not available in the response schema; example inputs are included here in details.

claims.summary: For every three signed 32-bit inputs, the export returns the first input bounded by the lower and upper inputs according to signed comparisons.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (if x.slt lo = true then lo else if hi.slt x = true then hi else x)]
claims.reason: The statement uses signed comparisons and returns the lower bound, upper bound, or input according to the stated conditions. When the bounds are reversed, it follows that same condition order (for example, clamp(5, 10, 0) returns 10).
claims.name: Examples.Toy.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `lo` below `lo`, `hi` above `hi`, else `x`.
details: Inputs: three 32-bit values, each interpreted as signed for comparisons.

The result is the lower bound if the first input is below it, the upper bound if the upper bound is below the first input, and otherwise the first input; it selects an existing input value, with no arithmetic wraparound.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping, with exactly the specified result.
caveats: The source's conditional notation is elaborated into comparisons with true; this preserves the intended signed comparisons.
The claim specifies only the returned value, not any other effects of execution.

claims.summary: For every pair of 32-bit inputs, the export returns their greatest common divisor when both are interpreted as unsigned values.
claims.statement:
∀ (a b : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Toy.Lifted.module "gcd" [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 a, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 b]
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 (BitVec.ofNat 32 (a.toNat.gcd b.toNat))]
claims.reason: For every pair of unsigned 32-bit inputs, the statement returns their natural-number gcd encoded as a 32-bit value, including gcd(a, 0) = a.
claims.name: Examples.Toy.gcd
claims.intent: `gcd(a, b)` on unsigned 32-bit ints: their greatest common divisor (`gcd(a, 0) = a`).
details: Inputs: two 32-bit values, each interpreted as unsigned.
The result is their natural-number greatest common divisor, encoded in 32 bits; there is no arithmetic wraparound affecting the result.
Returns additionally guarantees the module can be instantiated and every call under every host behavior terminates without trapping, with exactly the specified result.
caveats: Inputs are converted to unsigned natural numbers before taking the greatest common divisor; negative signed interpretations are not used.
The natural-number result is reduced to 32 bits, though the greatest common divisor of these inputs already fits in 32 bits.
